name: rotate-copy-straddle
source: mcweed airway port profile: 'rotating to -150 degrees BEFORE RotateCopy(3) put the cap circles across the -180 degree period boundary, dropping a chunk of each port.' RotateCopy/RotateCopyZ fold the query domain into one 360/n sector centred on 0 degrees.
summary: Three radial ports at 120 degree spacing with the first at -150 degrees. Pattern at canonical 0 then rotate the set; do not rotate the source first. NOTE ON THE LIBRARY: RotateCopyZ now auto-recenters (it infers the source angle from its bbox centre), so the literal incident code port.RotateZ(-150).RotateCopyZ(3) is now CORRECT for a simple radial port, and a source too wide for the sector panics loudly instead of aliasing. The failure that is still silent is the explicit-angle form, port.RotateZ(-150).RotateCopyAtZ(3, -150): RotateCopyAtZ assumes the source is already canonical, so the fold never reaches the pre-rotated source and all three ports disappear with no panic. That is what asfailed does. The same silent loss happens if the whole ring+port assembly is patterned (ring.Cut(port).RotateCopyZ(3)): a bbox centred on the Z axis skips both the recentre and the extent check.
